mechanism: Mark the six original joints along each wire that coincide in a genuine optimal five-unit overlap after a quarter turn and translation. Predict 6 by counting the six matched joint positions as six common length units, instead of the five intervals between them.
design_difference: Old preset6 summed incompatible four-edge U and two-edge run alignments; old preset4 used only a four-edge U. New design styles ONLY existing joint contours, identifies a different actually realizable optimal five-edge chain, and targets vertex-versus-segment counting. No old colored segment is reused as a cosmetic substitute.
primary_math_proof: For positive length overlap, orthogonal grid edges must be parallel, hence the relative rotation is a multiple of 90 degrees. At a fixed such orientation, horizontal overlap versus x-translation is piecewise linear with integer endpoint breakpoints; similarly vertically. Integer translations attain an optimum, also covering configurations with overlap in only one direction. Enumerating all eight D4 orientations and translations -12..12 proves maximum5; outside the bounded intersecting envelopes overlap is zero. A reflection-free witness T(x,y)=(2-y,x-5) matches wire1 edges1..5 to wire0 edges1..5. It aligns six existing joints1..6 but only five unit intervals. Recoloring circle borders preserves all18 black filled joints and sixteen unit segments.
